title: Dedicated deployment beta readiness checklist and KPI slate
content:
Purpose: This working doc collects the minimal operational checklist, KPI slate, contingency triggers, and signoff path for the upcoming dedicated-capacity beta. It is a product-ops working artifact intended to be pragmatic and actionable for the cross-functional launch team (product-ops, infra, serving-runtime, SRE, solutions-eng).

Scope: Applies to early dedicated customers participating in the 'dedicated beta' (reserved GPU pool delivered via Dedicated product). Focus areas: capacity planning, latency/cost KPIs, canary rollout plan, SLOs and alert thresholds, oncall staffing, rollback criteria, and post-launch evaluation. Not in scope: long-term pricing changes or contract negotiation details.

Quick summary (one-line): Greenlight candidate if p95 < 220ms for small-gen route, cost per 1k input tokens within target band, and autoscale ramp behaves within expected headroom during 2x stress test.

Key KPIs (tracked in the launch dashboard):
- Uptime (service reachable): target 99.95% for beta window (owner: SRE)
- Request success rate (2xx): target >= 99.6%
- p50/p95/p99 latencies (inference tail): p95 target <= 220ms for gen-small, <= 450ms for gen-large
- 95th percentile token latency (generation per-token): target <= 12ms per token on reserved A100 pool
- Mean QPS per GPU and GPU utilization: target utilization 60-75% in steady-state canary
- Autoscaler response time to CPU/GPU pressure: < 90s to add a node, < 3min to re-balance (infra owner: Platform Eng)
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): target >= 28% during steady traffic for repeat prompts
- Cost per 1k output tokens (approx): < $0.95 for gen-small on quantized model config
- Error class breakdown (model OOM, runtime OOM, network, auth): each category < 0.15% of requests
- Incidents/MTTR: < 1 P1 incident during beta trial, MTTR target < 20m for service-impacting issues (SRE + Infra)

Acceptance thresholds and go/no-go logic (owner: product-ops lead):
- Fast acceptance: All hard SLOs green for 24h during canary and stress window -> proceed to ramp to 10% customer traffic.
- Soft acceptance: Minor non-blocking alerts but compensating mitigations exist (cache tuning, temporary rate limit) -> proceed with caution and daily signoff.
- Blocker conditions: sustained p95 > threshold for 1h and no clear mitigation OR repeated OOMs across nodes OR autoscaler failing to add capacity -> rollback.

Canary rollout plan (timeline and owners):
- Day -7: Final infra smoke test (infra + serving-runtime). Validate autoscale, ephemeral node bootstrap, model load times. Owner: Platform Eng.
- Day -3: Closed canary with internal traffic (10% synthetic traffic matching production prompt profile). Owner: Solutions Eng.
- Day 0: Beta opens to 1 customer cohort (low QPS). Observe 6h tight-monitoring window. Owner: Customer Success + Product-Ops.
- Day 2: If green, increase to cohort + 2 customers (or 5% traffic). Continue 24h observation.
- Day 5-7: Stress test ramp to 2x expected steady state for 1h; evaluate thermal, OOM, autoscale behaviours. Owner: SRE.

Pre-launch checklist (checkbox style, owner and status notes):
- [ ] Capacity reservation verified and quotas applied (owner: infra) — comment: reservation request INF-REQ-022 submitted 2025-02-18.
- [ ] Model quantization profile validated end-to-end (owner: applied-ml) — test pass: gen-small q4_0.
- [ ] Canary alert playbook authored and reviewed (owner: product-ops) — included alert table and paging paths.
- [ ] Cost telemetry pipeline tests (billing events to usage pipeline) passed (owner: finance-eng) — test id: billing-dryrun-11.
- [ ] Customer onboarding docs and runbook for dedicated customers published (owner: solutions-eng) — doc link in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Disaster fallback: route to hosted API + customer opt-in for degraded SLA established (owner: product)

Operational triggers and immediate mitigations (for SRE/infra oncall):
- Trigger: p95 > target for 10m and rising -> Mitigate: temporarily reduce batch size by 25%, enable lower latency model variant, notify product-ops.
- Trigger: GPU OOM rate > 0.2% for 15m -> Mitigate: drop large-batch jobs, increase mem-swap pool, re-route heavy customers to other isolates.
- Trigger: Autoscaler fails to add node within 3m -> Mitigate: manual node spawn runbook, and fallback to dedicated reserve capacity or hosted API.
- Trigger: Cost burn > forecast by 20% within 24h window -> Mitigate: throttle low-priority tasks, increase sampling for embeddings, notify finance.

Staffing & rotations (initial 10-day beta window):
- Primary oncall (24/7): SRE rotation (assigned: Evan Brooks)
- Secondary (platform infra): Platform Eng (Diego Marquez)
- Model/Serving Lead (daytime): Rina Kapoor (08:00-18:00 PST)
- Product-ops duty lead (coordination + customer comms): Aisha Patel (oncall for major decisions)
- Escalation path: 1) SRE -> 2) Platform Eng -> 3) CTO on call (only for major P0 incidents)

Monitoring & dashboards (minimum required panels):
- Dedicated-beta-overview: uptime, p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization by pool, QPS per customer, cache hit rate.
- Cost-explorer-dedicated: rolling 24h cost delta vs forecast, cost per 1k tokens per model.
- Incident-triage: error-class breakdown, top failing routes, model load times.

Rollback decision rubric:
- Immediate rollback if any of: sustained p95 breach > 80% above target for 1h, repeated OOMs across 30%+ of nodes, critical autoscaler failures preventing capacity addition.
- Rollback procedure: 1) Stop traffic to dedicated pool (product-ops + solutions-eng), 2) Reroute customers to hosted endpoints, 3) Trigger postmortem ticket and hotfix plan.

Customer communication plan (templates + cadence):
- Pre-launch: 48h heads-up email + brief runbook of expected behavior and support channel.
- Incident: templated update at 15m, 1h, 3h with status, mitigation in-flight, ETA for recovery.
- Post-event: root-cause summary and next steps within 72h.

Risk register (top 6 items):
1) Model memory blowups on edge prompts -> mitigation: input length cap + better OOM detection.
2) Premature capacity exhaustion during spike -> mitigation: emergency reserved pool and throttles.
3) Billing mismatch -> mitigation: dry-run reconciliation and on-call finance contact.
4) Latency regressions after quant changes -> mitigation: A/B small internal traffic and rollback quant profile.
5) Onboarding confusion for customers -> mitigation: one-pager + 1:1 onboarding window.
6) Observability gaps -> mitigation: dashboard smoke tests and synthetic canaries.

Post-launch evaluation (day 7 / day 30 checkpoints):
- Day 7: Operational health check (SRE + infra), KPI status, list of incident tickets and mitigations, customer feedback roundup.
- Day 30: Cost vs forecast reconciliation, performance regression check vs baseline, recommended config changes for GA.

Appendix: quick sample KPI row format (copy into tracker sheet):
- metric_id, metric_name, target, measurement_window, owner, current_status, last_24h_value, notes
- kpi-01, p95-gen-small-ms, <=220, 24h rolling, eng-sre, amber, 237, elevated tail due to synthetic stress at 16:10
- kpi-02, token-cost-1k, <=0.95, 24h, finance-eng, green, 0.82, q4_0 quantization in use

Notes / open questions:
- Confirm whether customers should have the option to opt for autoscale-off reserved pools (some customers want guaranteed latency at fixed capacity).
- Finalize cost allocation mapping for multi-tenant telemetry before GA.

Next steps: assign owners to any unchecked pre-launch items, schedule day -7 smoke test, publish final canary playbook to Confluence and tie to the grafana dashboard for automated snapshots.

Document history: created 2025-02-10 by Aisha Patel, major edits 2025-03-03 (added staffing rotation and revised p95 targets).
